blocks.t: Mr. Patel had handed the worksheet out at the start of class. He had said, friends. We are doing one exercise today. We have been talking about the Compassionate Witness for three weeks. Today we are going to test her. The test is simple. I want you to write, in the left column, the actual sentences you said to yourself this week when something went wrong. Then I want you to imagine — and this is where most of you are going to do real work — I want you to imagine that your best friend came to you with the same situation, and I want you to write, in the right column, what you would have said to them.

blocks.t: One last thing. If, when you compare the two columns, the right column is much kinder than the left — that is the Friend Test. That is the gap we have been talking about. The Friend Test tells you, in the most direct possible way, that you are talking to yourself in a voice you would not let anybody else use on your friend.

blocks.t: The thing that went wrong this week was that I lost my temper at Aaliyah on Sunday. I did not call her names — I have not done that since fourth grade. But I said something sharp to her about a thing she had borrowed from my room and broken. The thing was small. It was a pen. I do not actually care about the pen. I was, in the moment, just frustrated about something else, and I took it out on her. She said I am sorry and walked away looking small. I have been carrying it since Sunday.

blocks.t: What I said to myself: you are a bad brother. You promised yourself when you were six, after the bike thing, that you would not do this kind of thing to Aaliyah. You have been doing it anyway. You are the thing you said you would not be. You are going to keep being it. The August 14 ice cream thing is a joke if you are going to act like this on a random Sunday in December.

He scratched that one out too. He was having, for the first time in his life, a very specific cognitive experience, and the experience was: I genuinely do not know how to be kind to myself.

blocks.t: When he tried, the words came out wrong. The words came out with a but attached. You apologized — but you still meant it when you said it. You are a good brother — but a good brother would not have said that. It was one moment — but it was a moment that revealed who you really are.

blocks.t: The but is the Critic.
blocks.h: The but is the Critic.

blocks.t: The Critic has spent twelve years getting good at sneaking buts into the sentence. The Critic knows that an outright attack will trigger Marcus's defenses. The Critic knows that a sneaky but will slide past the defenses and land in the soft part underneath. So the Critic delivers the Compassionate Witness's opening line, and then adds a but, and the whole sentence collapses back into self-punishment.

The Critic can mimic the Compassionate Witness, almost flawlessly, for the first six words, and then it does the thing.

blocks.t: You apologized, and that is what accountability looks like. You meant it when you said the sharp thing because you were twelve and frustrated, and that is what twelve-year-olds do when they are frustrated. You are allowed to make a mistake of that size and still be a person worth loving. You are not the worst thing you have ever said. You are the whole person, across years, who said one sharp thing on a Sunday in December and one kind thing on a Monday, and over time the average is going to be okay.

blocks.t: It does not feel quite true to Marcus yet. That is okay. He did not write it because it felt true. The believing is not the prerequisite to the writing.

blocks.t: You write the new sentence. You write it badly. You write it again. You write it a hundred times, in journal after journal, in moment after moment, until one day — and it will not feel like a single day, it will feel like a slow leak — the new sentence has become the more natural one, and the but has lost a little of its grip, and the Compassionate Witness is, for thirty seconds at a stretch, the louder voice.

blocks.t: It works. It really, actually works. Why did no one tell me this when I was younger, they say. Why did no one tell me when I was twelve.

blocks.t: This is what the Friend Test does, when you actually use it. It does not silence the Critic forever. The Critic is the Critic. The Friend Test gives you a way of asking, in the middle of self-flagellation, would I let anybody use these exact words on Aaliyah?
